consumer_interface: This page develops unitary braid actions on fixed-total-charge fusion spaces, then separates projective phase, logical block error, and leakage. It verifies the three-anyon Ising matrices directly and proves the multi-anyon Majorana Clifford restriction under an explicit channel-identification interface. For the fixed Fibonacci F/R convention, it verifies the three-anyon matrices and exact joint SU(5) × SU(8) density of the two six-strand path-matrix blocks using finite algebraic certificates. Triple-anyon encodings extend these conditional gates to arbitrary finite registers with explicit operator-norm, logical-error, and leakage bounds. The physical interface is conditional on a realized fusion space and its specified exchange action. No exact leakage-free entangler or useful joint braid-length bound is asserted; common braid phases must be tracked under coherent control. The QC25 Fibonacci data carrier supplies the coherent fixed-chirality model through an explicit exact verification of all simple-input pentagon and hexagon sectors; pair-charge and triple codes are compared inside that category without identifying their projectors. The Ising data carrier supplies only the three-anyon sector; the all-m Majorana channel identification is an explicit interface hypothesis, not a consequence claimed from that carrier.

consumer_interface:
## Definition

Let $V=V(x^n\to c)\ne0$ be the finite-dimensional fixed-total-charge fusion
space for $n$ identical charges $x$, equipped with the unitary fusion-tree
inner product from [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]]. Let
$\mathcal C=\mathbb C^k$ with its ordered orthonormal computational basis,
where $k\ge1$. A **fixed-charge encoding** is an isometry
$J:\mathcal C\to V$, so $J^*J=I_{\mathcal C}$. Its code subspace is
$J\mathcal C$, and its code projector is
$$P:=JJ^*:V\to V.$$
An encoding records a chosen subspace of a fusion space; it does not identify
that subspace with an object of the fusion category.
supplier_interface:
## Definition

Fix an ordered list of simple charges $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, a simple total charge
$d$, and a parenthesized binary fusion tree. At each internal vertex with
incoming charges $x,y$ and outgoing charge $z$, choose one vector from an
orthonormal basis of $V_{xy}^z$. An **admissible labeling** assigns a simple
charge to each internal edge so that each chosen vertex basis is nonempty; a
separate multiplicity-basis index is retained at every vertex. Compose the
vertex morphisms, inserting the associators required by the chosen tree, to
obtain a morphism from the parenthesized input tensor to $d$. These composite
morphisms are the **fusion-tree vectors**. The family is called a
**fusion-tree basis** when it is an orthonormal basis of the fixed-input,
fixed-total fusion space. For the empty input list the tensor is $\mathbf1$
and its empty tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$ when $d=\mathbf1$;
for one input $a_1$, the only tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{a_1}$ when
$d=a_1$. The next local lemma proves the basis property for every finite input
list and includes the dimension recursion ([[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]).

## Definition

Let $x$ be a simple charge in a unitary braided fusion category, let $n\ge2$,
and fix a total charge $c$ with nonzero multiplicity space
$V(x^n\to c)$. Use the left-associated fusion-tree basis. For the Artin
generator $\sigma_i$ that exchanges the $i$th and $(i+1)$st strands, let
$T_i$ be the specified sequence of $F$-moves that changes from the fixed tree
basis to a basis where those two charges fuse first, and let $R_i$ apply the
corresponding $R$-symbol on each pair-charge channel. Define
$$\rho_c(\sigma_i):=T_i^{-1}R_iT_i.$$
This defines the generator assignment. The next theorem proves that the
assignment descends from words to a well-defined group homomorphism. Word
products use matrix multiplication acting right-to-left on column vectors.
The abstract group in this definition is the Artin group
[[def-braid-group-by-the-artin-presentation]]; the positive crossing is the
generator convention used for the displayed $R$-symbols. If a motion is
described chronologically, its matrix product is written in reverse temporal
order.
supplier_interface:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

supplier_interface:
## Definition

Let $a,b,c,d$ be simple charges in a unitary fusion category, and put
$P_L=((a\otimes b)\otimes c)$ and $P_R=a\otimes(b\otimes c)$. The local
fusion-tree basis result [[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]] identifies

$$\mathcal H_L:=\bigoplus_e V_{ab}^e\otimes V_{ec}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d),$$

and

$$\mathcal H_R:=\bigoplus_f V_{bc}^f\otimes V_{af}^d \quad\text{with}\quad\operatorname{Hom}(P_R,d),$$

by the corresponding tree compositions. These direct sums carry the
orthonormal left- and right-tree bases. If $\mu:a\otimes b\to e$ and
$\nu:e\otimes c\to d$ are vertex basis maps, write
$L_{e,\mu,\nu}:=\nu\circ(\mu\otimes\operatorname{id}_c):P_L\to d$. If
$\rho:b\otimes c\to f$ and $\sigma:a\otimes f\to d$ are vertex basis maps,
write $R_{f,\rho,\sigma}:=\sigma\circ(\operatorname{id}_a\otimes\rho):P_R\to d$.
Let $\alpha_{a,b,c}:P_L\to P_R$ be the associator. Define the **F-symbol
matrix** $F_d^{abc}$ by

$$L_{e,\mu,\nu}\circ\alpha_{a,b,c}^{-1} =\sum_{f,\rho,\sigma}F_d^{abc}[(f,\rho,\sigma),(e,\mu,\nu)]R_{f,\rho,\sigma}.$$

Rows index target-tree labels and multiplicity indices; columns index
source-tree labels and multiplicity indices. The sums retain every fusion
channel and every multiplicity coordinate.
If the fixed-total fusion space is zero-dimensional, the F-symbol is the unique
empty $0\times0$ matrix.

## Definition

Let $a,b,c$ be simple objects in a unitary braided fusion category, with
braiding $c_{a,b}:a\otimes b\to b\otimes a$ as in [[def-braiding]]. The typed
channel-exchange map on $V_{ab}^c=\operatorname{Hom}(a\otimes b,c)$ is the
pullback

$$\mathcal R_{ab}^c(f):=f\circ c_{a,b}^{-1}\in V_{ba}^c.$$

Choose orthonormal bases in the two multiplicity spaces. The matrix of
$\mathcal R_{ab}^c$ in these bases is the **R-symbol** $R_{ab}^c$. This
pullback convention fixes the orientation of the coordinate exchange; reversing
the braiding orientation replaces it by the inverse convention. If the spaces
are zero-dimensional, the braiding isomorphism identifies both with $0$ and
the R-symbol is the unique empty $0\times0$ matrix.

## Definition

Let $m\ge2$ and let $\mathcal H=(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes m}$. A **Majorana
system of length $2m$** is a family of operators
$\gamma_1,\ldots,\gamma_{2m}\in\operatorname{End}(\mathcal H)$ satisfying
$$\gamma_j^*=\gamma_j,\qquad \gamma_j^2=I,\qquad \gamma_j\gamma_k=-\gamma_k\gamma_j\quad(j\ne k).$$
Its parity operator is $\Pi=i^m\gamma_1\cdots\gamma_{2m}$. For each adjacent
pair, put
$$Q_1(j)=\frac{I-i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad Q_\psi(j)=\frac{I+i\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}}2,\qquad U_j=\exp\!\left(-\frac\pi4\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1}\right).$$

A **Majorana–Ising exchange interface** on a fixed parity sector consists of
such a system, a choice $\eta\in\{1,-1\}$ and the sector
$\mathcal H_\eta=\ker(\Pi-\eta I)$, together with the following explicit
model-identification hypotheses for every $1\le j<2m$: the Ising pair-charge
projections are identified with $Q_1(j),Q_\psi(j)$, and the exchange is
$R_1Q_1(j)+R_\psi Q_\psi(j)$ with the same relative phase
$R_\psi/R_1=i$. The last identity is required for all adjacent pairs as part
of the interface; the three-anyon supplier below establishes it only in its
stated sector and does not prove this all-$m$ identification.
supplier_interface:
## Example

Use simple labels $\mathbf1,\psi,\sigma$ with unit fusion and
$\sigma\otimes\sigma=\mathbf1\oplus\psi$,
$\sigma\otimes\psi=\psi\otimes\sigma=\sigma$, and
$\psi\otimes\psi=\mathbf1$. In the three-$\sigma$, total-$\sigma$ fusion
space, the intermediate-channel basis is $(\mathbf1,\psi)$. In the pullback
R convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], fix

$$F^{\sigma\sigma\sigma}_{\sigma} =2^{-1/2}\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&-1\end{pmatrix},\qquad R^{\sigma\sigma}_{\mathbf1}=e^{-i\pi/8},\qquad R^{\sigma\sigma}_{\psi}=e^{3i\pi/8}.$$

These are sector data only. This item makes no claim about an all-label Ising
F/R table or global Ising ribbon coherence.

The phases above use the pullback convention in [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]]. In a
convention recording the eigenvalues of the object-level braiding itself, the
eigenvalues are the inverses of the displayed phases. This convention note
does not extend the sector data to any other Ising fusion space.
consumer_mentions:
[F1] In the three-$\sigma$, total-$\sigma$ Ising sector, the supplier gives
$R_1=e^{-i\pi/8}$ and $R_\psi=e^{3i\pi/8}$, hence
$R_\psi/R_1=i$. [[ex-qc-tqc-ising-data]]
consumer_fact_uses: 2.1 Since $(\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1})^2=-I$, expansion of the exponential gives $U_j=2^{-1/2}(I-\gamma_j\gamma_{j+1})$. Its restrictions to $\operatorname{ran}Q_1(j)$ and $\operatorname{ran}Q_\psi(j)$ are respectively $e^{-i\pi/4}I$ and $e^{i\pi/4}I$. Using the phase ratio in [F1] as imposed for every generator by the interface, the channel exchange equals $$R_1Q_1(j)+R_\psi Q_\psi(j)=R_1e^{i\pi/4}U_j.$$ Thus it differs from $U_j$ by one common scalar. [given, F1, algebra] ∎

## Definition

Assume the Fibonacci fusion rules
$1\otimes x=x\otimes1=x$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=1\oplus\tau$, with each
listed summand of multiplicity one. For six ordered $\tau$ charges, let
$W_a$ be the fixed-input, fixed-total fusion space of total charge
$a\in\{1,\tau\}$ in the tree that first fuses leaves $1,2,3$ and $4,5,6$
separately, then fuses those triple outputs. Let
$V_a$ be the same fixed-charge space in the left-associated tree.

To identify these spaces, write
$A=((\tau_1\otimes\tau_2)\otimes\tau_3)$. Use the object associator
composite
$$g=(\alpha^{-1}_{A\otimes\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6}) \circ\alpha^{-1}_{A,\tau_4,\tau_5\otimes\tau_6} \circ(\operatorname{id}_A\otimes\alpha_{\tau_4,\tau_5,\tau_6})$$

morphism $f$ into $a$, define $G_a(f)=f\circ g^{-1}:V_a$; this is a unitary
change of fusion-tree coordinates.

indexed by the charge $x\in\{1,\tau\}$ after the first two anyons: both
$x\otimes\tau\to\tau$ channels have multiplicity one. Write these vectors as
$|x\rangle$. For $x,y\in\{1,\tau\}$ and $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, let $|x,y;a\rangle$
be the grouped-tree vector with first triple path $x$, first triple total
$\tau$, second triple path $y$, second triple total $\tau$, and final vertex
channel $\tau\otimes\tau\to a$. The last channel has multiplicity one. Define
$$\mathcal C_a:=G_a\bigl(\operatorname{span}\{|x,y;a\rangle: x,y\in\{1,\tau\}\}\bigr)\subseteq V_a.$$

$(G_a|1,1;a\rangle,G_a|1,\tau;a\rangle,
G_a|\tau,1;a\rangle,G_a|\tau,\tau;a\rangle)$, the inclusion
$J_a:\mathbb C^4\to V_a$ is an isometry; its code projector is $P_a=J_aJ_a^*$.

## Definition

Fix an ordered list of simple charges $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, a simple total charge
$d$, and a parenthesized binary fusion tree. At each internal vertex with
incoming charges $x,y$ and outgoing charge $z$, choose one vector from an
orthonormal basis of $V_{xy}^z$. An **admissible labeling** assigns a simple
charge to each internal edge so that each chosen vertex basis is nonempty; a
separate multiplicity-basis index is retained at every vertex. Compose the
vertex morphisms, inserting the associators required by the chosen tree, to
obtain a morphism from the parenthesized input tensor to $d$. These composite
morphisms are the **fusion-tree vectors**. The family is called a
**fusion-tree basis** when it is an orthonormal basis of the fixed-input,
fixed-total fusion space. For the empty input list the tensor is $\mathbf1$
and its empty tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$ when $d=\mathbf1$;
for one input $a_1$, the only tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{a_1}$ when
$d=a_1$. The next local lemma proves the basis property for every finite input
list and includes the dimension recursion ([[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]).

## Statement

Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be simple charges, let $d$ be a simple total charge, and
fix any parenthesized binary tree $T$ on the ordered input list. The fusion-tree
vectors of [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]] form an orthonormal basis of
$\operatorname{Hom}(T,d)$. Their number is

$$m_T(d)=\sum_{\ell\,\mathrm{admissible}}\;\prod_{v\,\mathrm{internal}}N_{\ell(v_L)\,\ell(v_R)}^{\ell(v)},$$

where the leaves carry the inputs, the root carries $d$, and each internal edge
is labeled by a simple charge. For the left-associated tree on $n$ inputs this
gives $m_0(d)=1$ if $d=\mathbf1$ and $0$ otherwise,
$m_1(d)=1$ if $a_1\cong d$ and $0$ otherwise, and

$$m_n(d)=\sum_e m_{n-1}(e)N_{e a_n}^d\qquad(n\ge2).$$

## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules

its one-dimensional multiplicity space. On simple-label blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.

every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

## Definition

Fix an ordered list of simple charges $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, a simple total charge
$d$, and a parenthesized binary fusion tree. At each internal vertex with
incoming charges $x,y$ and outgoing charge $z$, choose one vector from an
orthonormal basis of $V_{xy}^z$. An **admissible labeling** assigns a simple
charge to each internal edge so that each chosen vertex basis is nonempty; a
separate multiplicity-basis index is retained at every vertex. Compose the
vertex morphisms, inserting the associators required by the chosen tree, to
obtain a morphism from the parenthesized input tensor to $d$. These composite
morphisms are the **fusion-tree vectors**. The family is called a
**fusion-tree basis** when it is an orthonormal basis of the fixed-input,
fixed-total fusion space. For the empty input list the tensor is $\mathbf1$
and its empty tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$ when $d=\mathbf1$;
for one input $a_1$, the only tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{a_1}$ when
$d=a_1$. The next local lemma proves the basis property for every finite input
list and includes the dimension recursion ([[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]).

## Example

Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel, use the standard unit-vector inclusion as the orthonormal basis of
its one-dimensional multiplicity space. On simple-label blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

supplier_interface:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

$$m_n(d)=\sum_e m_{n-1}(e)N_{e a_n}^d\qquad(n\ge2).$$

over all intermediate simple charges and multiplicity indices of the products
of the corresponding F- and R-block entries.

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$. In the normalized Fibonacci B6 representation on
$V(\tau^6\to1)\cong\mathbb C^5$, the closure of the braid image in $U(5)$

supplier_interface:
## Example

Take the skeletal complex-linear category whose simple labels are
$\mathbf1,\tau$ and whose objects are finite direct sums of them, including
the empty direct sum $0$. For objects
$A=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus m_s}$ and $B=\bigoplus_s s^{\oplus n_s}$, set
$\operatorname{Hom}(A,B)=\bigoplus_s\operatorname{Mat}_{n_s\times m_s}(\mathbb C)$;
composition is block-matrix multiplication, dagger is conjugate transpose,
and the norm is the maximum of the operator norms of its blocks. Thus direct
sums are orthogonal. Define tensor product on simple labels by the fusion rules
$\mathbf1\otimes a=a\otimes\mathbf1=a$ and $\tau\otimes\tau=\mathbf1\oplus\tau$,
and extend it distributively to direct sums. For each allowed simple fusion
channel, use the standard unit-vector inclusion as the orthonormal basis of
its one-dimensional multiplicity space. On simple-label blocks, tensor a pair
of morphism matrices by their Kronecker product on multiplicity coordinates
and by the identity on each simple fusion channel; extend over direct sums.
This defines a bifunctor compatible with dagger. Use the strict unit gauge:
every F or R coordinate involving $\mathbf1$ is the identity. Put

$$\phi=\frac{1+\sqrt5}{2},\qquad u=\phi^{-1},\qquad v=\phi^{-1/2}.$$

The only nontrivial associator blocks are

$$F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=[1],\qquad F^{\tau\tau\tau}_{\tau}=\begin{pmatrix}u&v\\v&-u\end{pmatrix},$$

in the intermediate-channel order $(\mathbf1,\tau)$. In the pullback R
convention of [[def-qc-tqc-r-symbol]], the exchange blocks are

$$R^{\tau\tau}_{\mathbf1}=x=e^{-4\pi i/5},\qquad R^{\tau\tau}_{\tau}=y=e^{3\pi i/5}.$$

Because these are pullback symbols, define the object-level braiding
$c_{\tau,\tau}$ on the $\mathbf1$ and $\tau$ summands by $x^{-1}$ and
$y^{-1}$, respectively. Every braiding with a unit input is the strict
identity. These fixed chiral data define the Fibonacci unitary braided fusion
category in this gauge; the verification checks every nontrivial pentagon and
hexagon sector.

and fixes $R_\tau/R_1=e^{-3\pi i/5}$ and the displayed unitary $F$ block in

The five paths in $\mathcal P_1$ therefore decompose by the charge of the first three strands as one dimension from charge $1$, and $2\cdot2=4$ dimensions from charge $\tau$: the latter are two copies of the same two-dimensional three-strand block. On the first summand $C:=B_1B_2^{-1}$ is $1$. On each two-dimensional summand, $B_1=\operatorname{diag}(1,r)$ and $B_2=FB_1F$ with $F^2=I$, so direct multiplication gives $\det C=1$ and $\operatorname{tr}C=r+r^{-1}+(2-r-r^{-1})u^2=u^2=\phi^{-2}$; the last equality uses $u^2+u=1$, since $(2+u)u^2=1$. Consequently the full spectrum is $1,e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta}$, with the last two eigenvalues each repeated twice and $2\cos\theta=\phi^{-2}$. [F1, F7, F8, A2, algebra]

## Statement

Let $a_1,\ldots,a_n$ be simple charges, let $d$ be a simple total charge, and
fix any parenthesized binary tree $T$ on the ordered input list. The fusion-tree
vectors of [[def-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-basis]] form an orthonormal basis of
$\operatorname{Hom}(T,d)$. Their number is

$$m_T(d)=\sum_{\ell\,\mathrm{admissible}}\;\prod_{v\,\mathrm{internal}}N_{\ell(v_L)\,\ell(v_R)}^{\ell(v)},$$

where the leaves carry the inputs, the root carries $d$, and each internal edge
is labeled by a simple charge. For the left-associated tree on $n$ inputs this
gives $m_0(d)=1$ if $d=\mathbf1$ and $0$ otherwise,
$m_1(d)=1$ if $a_1\cong d$ and $0$ otherwise, and

$$m_n(d)=\sum_e m_{n-1}(e)N_{e a_n}^d\qquad(n\ge2).$$

multiplicities over all admissible internal charges.

consumer_fact_uses: 1.1 The fusion rule and $F/R$ convention in [F8], together with recurrence [F7], give $\dim V(\tau^3\to1)=1$, $\dim V(\tau^3\to\tau)=2$, and $\dim V(\tau^4\to\tau)=3$. The eight paths in $\mathcal P_\tau$ thus decompose by the first-three-charge label: charge $1$ contributes $1\cdot2=2$ dimensions, and charge $\tau$ contributes $V(\tau^3\to\tau)\otimes V(\tau\otimes\tau^3\to\tau)$ of dimension $2\cdot3=6$. The operator $C:=B_1B_2^{-1}$ is identity on the first summand. On the two-dimensional first-three charge-$\tau$ factor it has determinant $1$ and trace $\phi^{-2}$, so the full spectrum of $C$ is $1$ with multiplicity $2$ and $e^{i\theta},e^{-i\theta}$ each with multiplicity $3$, where $2\cos\theta=\phi^{-2}$. [F1, F7, F8, A2, algebra]

## Statement

Assume $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$, $n\ge2$, and a total charge $c$ with
$V(\tau^n\to c)\ne0$. The code in $3n$ $\tau$ anyons factors as
$\mathcal C_n\cong(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$.
For any adjacent pair of encoded triples, any $U\in U(4)$, and any
$\delta>0$, one normalized six-strand braid induces an ambient operator
within $\delta$ of the code-preserving ideal extension of $U$ on the entire
fixed-charge space $V(\tau^{3n}\to c)$. Consequently its logical block error
and leakage amplitude are each at most $\delta$, uniformly over all
spectator fusion paths and states that already have a component outside the
code.
supplier_interface:
## Statement

Let $\mathcal C$ be a unitary braided fusion category. A finite list of simple
charges and total charge determines a fusion space in each parenthesization.
For a crossing word with underlying object map $b_\beta:P_L\to P_{L'}$, define
its action on the corresponding Hom spaces by
$f\mapsto f\circ b_\beta^{-1}$, from $\operatorname{Hom}(P_L,d)$ to
$\operatorname{Hom}(P_{L'},d)$. Let $U_\beta$ be its matrix in chosen
fusion-tree bases. If each multiplicity basis is changed by the unitary
gauge matrices of [[def-qc-tqc-gauge-transform]], and $G_L,G_{L'}$ are the
induced source and target tree-basis unitaries, then

$$U_\beta'=G_{L'}^{-1}U_\beta G_L.$$

In particular, when $n\ge2$ and all $n$ strand charges are the same simple object $a$,
the adjacent exchanges act on the same fixed-total fusion space
$V=\operatorname{Hom}(a^{\otimes n},d)$, satisfy the Artin relations, and
define a unitary representation $\rho:B_n\to U(V)$, where $U(V)$ is the group
of invertible linear maps preserving the inner product on $V$.
If $V=0$, this is the unique action on the zero-dimensional space.
In that case $\rho'(\beta)=G_L^{-1}\rho(\beta)G_L$ for every braid $\beta$.
Thus basis-dependent matrix entries change, while the braid action up to
unitary equivalence and consistently transformed expectation values do not.
consumer_mentions:
[F3] A local braid on a tensor factor acts as its braid operator tensored with
the identity on spectator factors; unitary fusion-tree reassociation changes
basis by a unitary.
[[thm-qc-tqc-gauge-covariance]]
consumer_fact_uses: 1.1 Each triple has fusion factor $V(\tau^3\to\tau)\cong\mathbb C^2$. Associating the $n$ triple charges first gives the code factorization $(\mathbb C^2)^{\otimes n}\otimes V(\tau^n\to c)$; the second factor records all spectator fusion paths. This is an orthogonal fusion-tree decomposition by [F1, F3]. [given, F1, F3, construct]

1.2 Reassociate so the chosen adjacent six strands are first. Their total charge is $a\in\{1,\tau\}$, giving the orthogonal ambient decomposition $$V(\tau^{3n}\to c)\cong \bigoplus_{a=1,\tau}V(\tau^6\to a)\otimes V(a\otimes\tau^{3n-6}\to c).$$ The second factor contains every remaining fusion path and every multiplicity of the spectator triples. By [F3], a local six-strand braid $b$ acts as $\bigoplus_a\rho_a(b)\otimes I$ in this decomposition. [given, F3, algebra]

3.1 Tensoring an operator $A$ with a spectator identity preserves its norm: expand a vector in an orthonormal spectator basis to get $\|(A\otimes I)\xi\|^2=\sum_j\|A\xi_j\|^2\le\|A\|_{\mathrm{op}}^2\|\xi\|^2$, with equality on a maximizing unit vector tensored with one basis vector. The norm of an orthogonal direct sum is the maximum of the block norms, because the squared norm is the sum of the squared block norms. Hence $\|\rho(b)-\mathcal W\|_{\mathrm{op}}\le\delta$ on the whole ambient space. [F1, F3, step 2.1, algebra]

## Example

The exact B6 certificates have determinants $17$ and $22$ modulo $31$ for
the selected $24\times24$ and $63\times63$ Lie-word minors. In the
total-charge-$1$ six-anyon space there are two natural four-dimensional code
choices: a pair-charge code and the triple code of
[[def-qc-tqc-six-anyon-encoded-subspace]]. The density argument applies to
either chosen subspace; the two definitions use different fusion trees, and
no equality of their projectors is asserted. For a circuit with $G>0$ ideal
one-qubit or adjacent two-qubit gates, assigning $\delta_j=\epsilon/G$
gives total logical block error and leakage at most $\epsilon$.
supplier_interface:
## Definition

Fix an ordered list of simple charges $a_1,\ldots,a_n$, a simple total charge
$d$, and a parenthesized binary fusion tree. At each internal vertex with
incoming charges $x,y$ and outgoing charge $z$, choose one vector from an
orthonormal basis of $V_{xy}^z$. An **admissible labeling** assigns a simple
charge to each internal edge so that each chosen vertex basis is nonempty; a
separate multiplicity-basis index is retained at every vertex. Compose the
vertex morphisms, inserting the associators required by the chosen tree, to
obtain a morphism from the parenthesized input tensor to $d$. These composite
morphisms are the **fusion-tree vectors**. The family is called a
**fusion-tree basis** when it is an orthonormal basis of the fixed-input,
fixed-total fusion space. For the empty input list the tensor is $\mathbf1$
and its empty tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{\mathbf1}$ when $d=\mathbf1$;
for one input $a_1$, the only tree vector is $\operatorname{id}_{a_1}$ when
$d=a_1$. The next local lemma proves the basis property for every finite input
list and includes the dimension recursion ([[lem-qc-tqc-fusion-tree-dimension]]).

supplier_interface:
## Definition

Let $\mathcal C$ be a fusion category over $\mathbb C$ in the sense of
[[def-fusion-and-multifusion-category]]. A **dagger structure** assigns to every
morphism $f:X\to Y$ a morphism $f^\dagger:Y\to X$, conjugate-linearly, with
$(g\circ f)^\dagger=f^\dagger\circ g^\dagger$ and
$(f^\dagger)^\dagger=f$. A **unitary fusion category** is such a fusion
category equipped with this dagger so that every morphism space is a
finite-dimensional normed space, composition is submultiplicative,
$\|f^\dagger\|=\|f\|$, and $\|f^\dagger f\|=\|f\|^2$. Thus each
$\operatorname{End}_{\mathcal C}(X)$ is a finite-dimensional $C^*$-algebra.
Positive endomorphisms are the elements of its usual $C^*$-positive cone
(equivalently $u^\dagger u$ for an endomorphism $u$); in particular, if $c$ is
simple and $\operatorname{End}(c)=\mathbb C\operatorname{id}_c$, then
$\lambda\operatorname{id}_c$ is positive exactly when $\lambda\ge0$. For any
morphism $f:X\to Y$, $f^\dagger f$ is positive in $\operatorname{End}(X)$;
also require $f^\dagger f=0$ to imply $f=0$. Semisimple direct-sum
decompositions can be chosen orthogonally:
their inclusions $i_j$ satisfy $i_j^\dagger i_k=0$ for $j\ne k$,
$i_j^\dagger i_j=\operatorname{id}$, and $\sum_j i_j i_j^\dagger=\operatorname{id}$.
Tensor product preserves daggers:
$(f\otimes g)^\dagger=f^\dagger\otimes g^\dagger$. Its associator and unit
constraints are **unitary**, meaning $\alpha^\dagger=\alpha^{-1}$,
$\lambda^\dagger=\lambda^{-1}$, and $\rho^\dagger=\rho^{-1}$.

The underlying fusion category is rigid, so its evaluation and coevaluation
morphisms satisfy the duality zig-zag identities. Those morphisms are not
required to be unitary isomorphisms. A braiding is additional structure; when
it is specified as a **unitary braiding**, each component satisfies
$c_{X,Y}^\dagger=c_{X,Y}^{-1}$. Positivity and unitarity are extra structure,
not consequences of the fusion rules or of the braid relations alone.

consumer_interface:
## Statement

Let $R$, $\delta$, $n$, $t$ and $W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ be as in [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]]. For link states $x,y$, let $x^*$ denote reflection across a horizontal line. The diagram $y\circ x^*:t\to t$ is either $\delta^c1_t$ for some $c\ge0$ or has fewer than $t$ propagating components. Define $\phi_{n,t}(x,y)=\delta^c$ in the first case and $0$ in the second, and extend $R$-bilinearly. Then $\phi_{n,t}$ is symmetric and satisfies

$$\phi_{n,t}(x\cdot a,y)=\phi_{n,t}(x,y\cdot a^*)$$

for all $x,y\in W_{n,t}(R,\delta)$ and $a\in\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$. Here $a^*$ is reflection across a horizontal line. The matrix of $\phi_{n,t}$ in the link-state basis is the Gram matrix obtained by reflecting and capping two link states, with one factor $\delta$ for each closed loop.
supplier_interface:
## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

supplier_interface:
## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

consumer_fact_uses: 1.1 Propagation cannot increase under stacking, and the identity is the only fully propagating diagram. Hence the nonidentity span is an ideal and the identity-coefficient map $\varepsilon$ is multiplicative. By [F2] its kernel is spanned by nonempty generator words. If $d_i e=0$ and $\varepsilon(e)=1$, [F2] gives $ae=\varepsilon(a)e$ for every $a$, so $e^2=e$ follows already from these linear equations. Reflect diagrams to obtain an algebra anti-involution $*$ fixing the generators and preserving $\varepsilon$: reflection reverses stacking and preserves each loop, so it has these properties by [F1]. Then $f=ee^*$ is annihilated on both sides by every $d_i$, has augmentation $1$, and is idempotent by the first observation. Since $f$ is right annihilated, $fe=\varepsilon(e)f=f$; since $e$ is left annihilated, $fe=\varepsilon(f)e=e$. Thus $e=f$ is itself two-sided. If $e,e'$ are two normalized two-sided annihilators, the same generator-word argument gives $ee'=e$ and $ee'=e'$, proving uniqueness. [F1, F2, given, construct, algebra]

1.3 For the converse construction use first the indeterminate $q$ and $L=\mathbb Q(q)$. Every positive quantum integer is nonzero in $L$. There is a normalized two-sided annihilator $p_n$ over $L$, as the following algebraic induction proves. Start with $p_0=p_1=1$ and $p_2=1-\delta^{-1}d_1$. Given $p_r$, put $P=p_r\otimes1$, $Q_0=p_{r-1}\otimes1\otimes1$, $a=d_{r-1}$, $b=d_r$, and $\mu=[r-1]/[r]$. The preceding recursion says $P=Q_0-\mu Q_0aQ_0$, while $Q_0^2=Q_0$, $PQ_0=Q_0P=P$, $Q_0b=bQ_0$ and $bab=b$. Consequently $bPb=(\delta-\mu)Q_0b=([r+1]/[r])Q_0b$. For $X=PbP$, this gives $X^2=([r+1]/[r])X$. Therefore $p_{r+1}=P-([r]/[r+1])X$ is idempotent, annihilates $b$ on both sides by the displayed sandwich identity, and annihilates every earlier generator because $P$ does. Every correction term has fewer than $r+1$ propagating strands, so its identity coefficient is zero and $\varepsilon(p_{r+1})=1$. The initial rank-two verification uses $d_1^2=\delta d_1$; the induction step applies for $r\ge2$. This proves the claim at every rank without using a complex-field theorem outside its hypotheses. [F1, F2, F4, construct, algebra]

3.1 The computation of steps 1.2–2.1 over $L$ now determines the entire matrix of $p_n$: its weight-$k$ block is $v_kv_k^{\mathsf T}/G_{n,k}(q^2)$. Let $S$ be the subring of $L$ generated by $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$ and all $G_{n,k}(q^2)^{-1}$, $0\le k\le n$. That displayed matrix $P_n$ has all entries in $S$. Apply the integral linear left inverse of [F3], after base change to $S$, to obtain $z\in\mathrm{TL}_n(S,q+q^{-1})$. Over $L$ it equals $p_n$, since $P_n=\rho_n(p_n)$. Since both $S$ and its free diagram module inject into their scalar extensions to $L$, it follows already over $S$ that $\rho_n(z)=P_n$, $\varepsilon(z)=1$, $z^2=z$, and $d_iz=zd_i=0$. This is the precise integrality step: no unproved centralizer or arbitrary-characteristic Schur–Weyl assertion is being used. [F1, F3, step 1.2, step 2.1, step 1.3, construct, algebra]

5.1 For a general field $K$, adjoin a root of $X^2-\delta X+1$ using [F5] if needed. This gives a field extension $K'$, with a nonzero root and the same polynomial values $B_{n,k}(\delta)$. Necessity follows in $K'$ by step 2.1. For sufficiency, step 4.1 gives a solution over $K'$ to the finite linear system $d_ie=0$, $\varepsilon(e)=1$ in diagram coefficients. Row reduction over $K$ shows that a linear system with coefficients and constants in $K$ is consistent over $K$ whenever it is consistent over a field extension: an inconsistent row $0=1$ would persist over that extension, while a row-echelon system without such a row has a solution by setting free variables to zero. Choose such a $K$-solution. Step 1.1 then proves its idempotence, both-sided annihilation and uniqueness. Ranks zero and one give the identity, with all the displayed quantum binomials equal to $1$. This completes both implications over every field. [F1, F5, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 4.1, construct, algebra] ∎

## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.

1.2 Suppose $\kappa\ge2$. By [F5], there is an integer $m\ge1$ with $t+1=m\kappa$. Fix a root $q_0=q$ and write $\epsilon=q_0^{m\kappa}\in\{1,-1\}$. For any $j$ not divisible by $\kappa$, $[j]_{q_0}\ne0$ and $[m\kappa+j]_{q_0}=\epsilon[j]_{q_0}$, by substituting $q_0^{m\kappa}=q_0^{-m\kappa}=\epsilon$ in the quantum-integer formula. supplier_interface:
## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, let $\delta\in R$, and let $n\ge0$. Let $t$ be an integer with $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even. The diagram module $M_R(n,t)$ has $n$ bottom boundary points and $t$ top boundary points, with stacking and loop removal as in [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. A component of a basis diagram is **propagating** if it meets both the bottom and top boundaries. Write $\operatorname{prop}(D)$ for the number of propagating components of a diagram $D:n\to t$.

Let $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ be the $R$-span of the basis diagrams $D:n\to t$ with $\operatorname{prop}(D)<t$. Define the **Temperley–Lieb link-state standard module**

$$W_{n,t}(R,\delta):=M_R(n,t)/M_R^{<t}(n,t).$$

Write $T_{n,t}$ for the set of diagrams in $\mathcal D(n,t)$ with exactly $t$ propagating components. The cosets of these diagrams form an $R$-basis of $W_{n,t}$. Identifying each diagram with its bottom arcs and defects gives a partial matching of the $n$ ordered bottom sites, with the additional condition that the $t$ unpaired sites are joined to the ordered top sites by noncrossing propagating strands. In particular, no defect lies inside an arc. The unpaired sites are called **defects**. Thus $t$ is the defect or through-line number; in sources using $p$ for the number of arcs, $p=(n-t)/2$.

The intended right action of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$, where $x\in M_R(n,t)$, $a\in M_R(n,n)$, and $x\circ a$ stacks $x$ above $a$. The submodule $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ is stable under this action, so it descends to $W_{n,t}$; the complete well-definedness argument is [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-module-action-is-well-defined]].

If $a,c$ are perfect matchings, their overlay is a disjoint union of $C(a,c)\ge1$ alternating cycles, counting a shared arc as a two-edge cycle; therefore $\phi_b(a,c)=b^{C(a,c)}$. Define the bilinear form $\phi'(a,c)=\left.\frac{d}{db}\phi_b(a,c)\right|_{b=0}.$ It follows that $\phi'(a,c)=1$ when $C(a,c)=1$ and $0$ when $C(a,c)>1$. [F1, F3, given, construct]

2.1 Delete site $2p$ and its incident arc from a perfect matching, and declare its partner to be the single defect. This is a bijection from perfect matchings on $2p$ sites to the link-state basis of $W_{2p-1,1}$: the inverse joins the unique defect to the appended site $2p$. For a pair $a,c$, deleting the two arcs incident to site $2p$ turns exactly the overlay cycle containing that site into the open path between the defects and leaves the other $C(a,c)-1$ cycles unchanged. Hence the ordinary one-defect Gram value of the images is $b^{C(a,c)-1}$, whose value at $b=0$ equals $\phi'(a,c)$. Thus the matrix of $\phi'$ is exactly the Gram matrix of $W_{2p-1,1}(\mathbb C,0)$. [F1, F3, step 1.1, construct]

3.2 For two link states $x,y$ on $2p$ sites with two defects, define $D_{x,y}$ to be the Temperley–Lieb diagram whose bottom arcs are those of $x$, whose top arcs are those of $y$, and whose two unmatched bottom sites are joined to the two unmatched top sites in left-to-right order by propagating strands. This matching is planar and is an allowed basis diagram. Let $x'$ and $y'$ be the perfect matchings obtained by joining the two defects of $x$ and $y$, respectively. If $z$ is a basis perfect matching and $C(y',z)$ is the number of cycles in the overlay of $y'$ and $z$, stacking $z$ above $D_{x,y}$ leaves the bottom matching $x'$ and removes exactly $C(y',z)-1$ closed cycles. Therefore $z\cdot D_{x,y}=\delta^{C(y',z)-1}x'$, where the coefficient at $\delta=0$ is defined as $1$ when $C(y',z)=1$ and $0$ when $C(y',z)>1$. This coefficient is exactly $\phi'(y',z)$, so $z\cdot D_{x,y}=\phi'(y',z)x'$. The same equality holds for every $z$ by linearity. [F1, F2, F3, F6, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 Let $z\ne0$. Nondegeneracy of $\phi'$ gives a nonzero functional $\phi'(-,z)$, so at least one perfect-matching basis vector $y'$ has $\phi'(y',z)\ne0$. For any target basis matching $x'$, cut from $x'$ and $y'$ the arcs incident to site $2p$ to obtain two-defect link states $x,y$. By step 3.2, $z\cdot D_{x,y}$ is a nonzero scalar multiple of $x'$. Thus the submodule generated by $z$ contains every basis vector and equals $W_{2p,0}$. Every nonzero submodule contains such a $z$, so the module is simple. ## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, let $\delta\in R$, and let $n\ge0$. Let $t$ be an integer with $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even. The diagram module $M_R(n,t)$ has $n$ bottom boundary points and $t$ top boundary points, with stacking and loop removal as in [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. A component of a basis diagram is **propagating** if it meets both the bottom and top boundaries. Write $\operatorname{prop}(D)$ for the number of propagating components of a diagram $D:n\to t$.

Let $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ be the $R$-span of the basis diagrams $D:n\to t$ with $\operatorname{prop}(D)<t$. Define the **Temperley–Lieb link-state standard module**

$$W_{n,t}(R,\delta):=M_R(n,t)/M_R^{<t}(n,t).$$

Write $T_{n,t}$ for the set of diagrams in $\mathcal D(n,t)$ with exactly $t$ propagating components. The cosets of these diagrams form an $R$-basis of $W_{n,t}$. Identifying each diagram with its bottom arcs and defects gives a partial matching of the $n$ ordered bottom sites, with the additional condition that the $t$ unpaired sites are joined to the ordered top sites by noncrossing propagating strands. In particular, no defect lies inside an arc. The unpaired sites are called **defects**. Thus $t$ is the defect or through-line number; in sources using $p$ for the number of arcs, $p=(n-t)/2$.

The intended right action of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$, where $x\in M_R(n,t)$, $a\in M_R(n,n)$, and $x\circ a$ stacks $x$ above $a$. The submodule $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ is stable under this action, so it descends to $W_{n,t}$; the complete well-definedness argument is [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-module-action-is-well-defined]].

Its initial ascending block is either $h_r$ or contains no $d_n$, and every later block lies in $A_n$. The surjection from the presented algebra to the diagram algebra is supplied by the local relations, so this spanning assertion applies to diagram words. Next, if $d$ has its largest adjacent arc at $s\ge r$, write $d=d_sf$. For $n\ge3$ this can be done without division: move the endpoint immediately outside that adjacent arc through the arc, so applying $d_s$ restores $d$ and creates no loop. If $s=1$ use site $3$; otherwise use site $s-1$. The outside site is either a defect or an endpoint of another arc, and reconnecting its former partner supplies the inverse state $f$. Now the relations give $h_r\otimes d=h_{s+2}\otimes d_r\cdots d_{s-1}d$. The latter state is $(s+2)$-admissible: the adjacent arc at $s$ has moved to $r$, all intervening endpoints shift by two, and the tail beyond $s+1$ still has no adjacent arc. Repetition, increasing $r$, proves spanning. At $n=1,2$ the same conclusion is checked on the at most two states, except $n=2,p=1,\delta=0$, when the needed factorization $d=d_1f$ fails. 3.1 Compute $F_n$ on the state $z_p$ with adjacent arcs $(1,2),(3,4),\ldots,(2p-1,2p)$ and all remaining sites defects. ## Statement

Let $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $n\ge0$, and $0\le p\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Put $t=n-2p$, and let $G_{n,p}$ be the Gram matrix of the link-state form on $W_{n,t}(\mathbb C,\delta)$ in its link-state basis. Set

$$d_{n,r}=\binom nr-\binom n{r-1},\qquad \binom n{-1}=0.$$

Then

$$\det G_{n,p}=\prod_{j=1}^{p}\left(\frac{[n-2p+1+j]_q}{[j]_q}\right)^{d_{n,p-j}}.$$

## Statement

For every $n\ge0$, each basis diagram in $\mathcal D(n,n)$ is a finite product of the elementary diagrams $d_1,\ldots,d_{n-1}$ from [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. The product can be chosen so that no intermediate stack creates a closed cycle. Therefore the set of diagrams lies in the unital subalgebra of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ generated by these diagrams.

Expanding with [F1] gives $g_i^{-1}=q^{-1/2}1-q^{1/2}d_i$ and $g_ig_{i+1}g_i=g_{i+1}g_ig_{i+1}$. Let $T_n:A_{n+1}\to A_n$ close the last top endpoint to the last bottom endpoint externally on the right, removing any resulting loop with factor $\delta$. Every summand of $M_n$ has an even total number of square-root factors, so $F_n$ has coefficients in $\mathbb Z[q,q^{-1}]$, independent of the chosen square root. [F1, given, construct, algebra]

Now the relations give $h_r\otimes d=h_{s+2}\otimes d_r\cdots d_{s-1}d$. The latter state is $(s+2)$-admissible: the adjacent arc at $s$ has moved to $r$, all intervening endpoints shift by two, and the tail beyond $s+1$ still has no adjacent arc. e\pm1$, and $z_p$ is as in step 3.1. In the induced basis the coefficient of $h_{2p+1}\otimes z_p$ in $F_{n+1}(1\otimes z_p)$ is $(-1)^n(\delta^2-4)

e0$ by inserting $\delta^{-1}d_{2j-1}$ at each initial cup. The resulting coefficient identity extends to $\delta=0$: the induced basis reduction in step 1.2 uses no division, so its matrices, and this coefficient, are Laurent polynomials in $q$. Finally $\delta^2-4=(q-q^{-1})^2
e0$. [F1, F4, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 1.2, step 5.1, algebra]

$$f_{n,p}=q^{n-2p+1}+q^{-(n-2p+1)}.$$
When $q\ne\pm1$ and $(n,p)$ is noncritical, restriction splits as $V_{n,p}\downarrow=V_{n-1,p}\oplus V_{n-1,p-1}$. Except at $(n,p,\delta)=(2,1,0)$, induction has a natural exact sequence
$$0\longrightarrow V_{n+1,p+1}\longrightarrow V_{n,p}\uparrow\longrightarrow V_{n+1,p}\longrightarrow0,$$
which splits when $(n,p)$ is noncritical. Here induction of a right module means $V\otimes_{A_n}A_{n+1}$.

If $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)\ge2$ and $p<p'$ are a pair reflected in a single intervening critical line, meaning $0<p'-p<\kappa$ and $p=p'+r(n,p')-\kappa$, then
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{A_n}(V_{n,p},V_{n,p'})\ne0.$$
Out-of-range standard modules are zero. Statements about a splitting omit zero summands.

## Statement

Let $q\in\mathbb C^\times$, $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, $n\ge0$, and $0\le p\le\lfloor n/2\rfloor$. Put $t=n-2p$, and let $G_{n,p}$ be the Gram matrix of the link-state form on $W_{n,t}(\mathbb C,\delta)$ in its link-state basis. Set

$$d_{n,r}=\binom nr-\binom n{r-1},\qquad \binom n{-1}=0.$$

Then

$$\det G_{n,p}=\prod_{j=1}^{p}\left(\frac{[n-2p+1+j]_q}{[j]_q}\right)^{d_{n,p-j}}.$$

The empty product for $p=0$ is $1$. The right side is interpreted as its polynomial continuation in $\delta$ at parameter values where an individual displayed quotient has a removable zero-over-zero form.

consumer_fact_uses: 1.1 First work at generic $q$. The rightmost-defect submodule has nondegenerate form by [F2], so its orthogonal complement is invariant and maps isomorphically to the restriction quotient. The smaller standards are simple by their rank-one diagram operators; an invariant form on such a standard is a scalar multiple of its nondegenerate standard form, because their associated maps into the dual differ by an endomorphism, and an endomorphism of a finite-dimensional complex simple module is scalar (take any eigenvalue). Subtracting the submodule projection from quotient basis lifts gives a unitriangular Gram splitting $G_{n,p}=U^{\mathsf T}(G_{n-1,p}\oplus\alpha_{n,p}G_{n-1,p-1})U$. Compute its scalar as follows. Group the link states into the four types: $n,n-1$ both defects; $n$ a defect and $n-1$ on an earlier arc; $(n-1,n)$ an arc; and $n$ on an arc ending earlier than $n-1$. Put $A=G_{n-2,p}$, $B=G_{n-2,p-1}$ and write the smaller-rank matrix as $G_{n-1,p}=\left(\begin{smallmatrix}A&AV_0\\V_0^{\mathsf T}A&V_0^{\mathsf T}AV_0+\alpha_{n-1,p}B\end{smallmatrix}\right)$. In the current off-diagonal Gram block the first column block is $(0,B)^{\mathsf T}$: types one and three have unmatched defects, while cutting the terminal arc in types two and three removes no closed component. The type-three diagonal block is $\delta B$, since the shared terminal arc closes one loop. If $(X,Y)^{\mathsf T}$ is the first column block of the projection coefficient matrix, multiplication by $G_{n-1,p}$ gives $AX+AV_0Y=0$ and $V_0^{\mathsf T}AX+(V_0^{\mathsf T}AV_0+\alpha_{n-1,p}B)Y=B$. Thus $X=-V_0Y$ and $Y=\alpha_{n-1,p}^{-1}I$. Its quadratic contribution is $\alpha_{n-1,p}^{-1}B$ after the four $V_0^{\mathsf T}AV_0$ terms cancel with coefficients $1-1-1+1$. Comparing the type-three block gives $\alpha_{n,p}=\delta-\alpha_{n-1,p}^{-1}$. At $n=2p$, deleting the terminal site closes exactly one additional component, so $G_{2p,p}=\delta G_{2p-1,p-1}$ and $\alpha_{2p,p}=\delta$. The recurrence solves to $\alpha_{n,p}=[n-2p+2]_q/[n-2p+1]_q$ by the quantum-integer recurrence. If the $A$ block is empty it is omitted; the same cancellation still holds. Its entries are rational functions regular at the root; subtracting this projection from each standard quotient lift gives a unitriangular splitting matrix $U$, also regular there. Since $F_{n-1}^*=F_{n-1}$ and the eigenvalues differ, the two summands are orthogonal. For generic $q$ this is exactly the orthogonal splitting just computed, since the submodule form is nondegenerate and its orthogonal complement is unique. Thus this Gram matrix identity is an identity of rational matrices regular at every noncritical root, and specializes there. This continuity argument applies to the entire matrix identity, rather than inferring a rank from a specialized determinant. [F2, F3, F4, F5, step 1.1, algebra]

## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.

Let $\ell<\infty$, let $n+1=A\ell$ and $m+1=B\ell$ with $0<B\le A$ and $n-m$ even. In characteristic zero, $W_{n,m}$ is simple. In characteristic $p>0$, write $B=p^v b'$ with $p\nmid b'$ and let $b\in\{1,\ldots,p-1\}$ be the residue of $b'$ modulo $p$. If
$$\left\lfloor\frac{A-B}{2}\right\rfloor<p^v(p-b),$$
then $W_{n,m}$ is simple. If $\ell=\infty$, every $W_{n,m}$ is simple. Also $W_{n,n-2}$ is simple whenever $[n]_\delta\ne0$.

## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit and $\delta\in R$. Define the quantum integers by

$$[0]_\delta=0,\qquad [1]_\delta=1,\qquad [r+1]_\delta=\delta[r]_\delta-[r-1]_\delta\quad(r\ge1).$$

The **quantum characteristic** of $(R,\delta)$ is the least positive integer $\ell$ with $[\ell]_\delta=0$, if one exists, and $\ell=\infty$ otherwise. No element of $R$ is inverted in this definition.

For $q\in\mathbb C^\times$ and $\delta=q+q^{-1}$, write $[r]_q=[r]_\delta$. If $q\ne\pm1$, this agrees with $(q^r-q^{-r})/(q-q^{-1})$; at $q=\pm1$ the recurrence gives $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}$. For complex-parameter classification, write $\kappa=\operatorname{ord}(q^2)$, with $\kappa=\infty$ when $q^2$ has infinite order. If $q\ne\pm1$, the quantum characteristic equals $\kappa$ when $\kappa<\infty$ and is $\infty$ otherwise. At $q=\pm1$, $\kappa=1$ but the complex quantum characteristic is $\infty$, because $[r]_q=rq^{r-1}\ne0$ for every positive $r$.

For a field $K$ of positive characteristic $p$, set $p(0)=1$ and, when $\ell<\infty$, set $p(i)=\ell p^{i-1}$ for $i\ge1$. In characteristic zero and finite $\ell$, the finite digit scale is $p(1)=\ell$; the separate characteristic-zero criterion below uses $a\ell-1$ for arbitrary positive integers $a$. If $\ell=\infty$, every finite index is already in the range $n<\ell$.

Hence substituting $\delta(t)$ in a nonzero polynomial gives a nonzero series, since otherwise the nonconstant series $\delta(t)$ would satisfy a polynomial over a field and therefore be constant in the algebraic closure of that field. Equivalently, factor the polynomial over an algebraic closure and note that each factor $\delta(t)-a$ is nonzero. Every quantum integer $[j]_{\delta(t)}$ is nonzero by its Laurent expression $q(t)^{1-j}(1-q(t)^{2j})/(1-q(t)^2)$, interpreted as a rational identity. ## Statement

Let $K$ be any field, $\delta\in K$, and let $0\le r\le n$ with $n-r$ even. Assume $r>0$ or $\delta\ne0$ or $n=r=0$. Put $A_n=\mathrm{TL}_n(K,\delta)$, use the right modules $W_{n,t}$ of [[def-temperley-lieb-link-state-standard-modules]], and put $D_{n,t}=W_{n,t}/\operatorname{rad}\phi_{n,t}$. There are $y,z:n\to r$ with $y\circ z^*=1_r$, and for $r>0$ both may be chosen as basis monic diagrams. There is an idempotent $e\in A_n$ with $eA_ne\cong A_r$ such that $M\mapsto Me$ is exact, sends $W_{n,t}$ to $W_{r,t}$, and sends $D_{n,t}$ to $D_{r,t}$, with value zero when $t>r$.

Consequently, for every allowed $m$,
$$[W_{n,m}:D_{n,r}]=[W_{r,m}:D_{r,r}],$$
where $W_{r,m}=0$ if $m>r$. The module $D_{r,r}=W_{r,r}$ is one dimensional and every diagram generator acts by zero. Thus the decomposition problem reduces exactly to multiplicities of this trivial module. The excluded case $n>r=0,\delta=0$ has $D_{n,0}=0$ and is not a simple label.

## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, let $\delta\in R$, and let $n\ge0$. Let $t$ be an integer with $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even. The diagram module $M_R(n,t)$ has $n$ bottom boundary points and $t$ top boundary points, with stacking and loop removal as in [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. A component of a basis diagram is **propagating** if it meets both the bottom and top boundaries. Write $\operatorname{prop}(D)$ for the number of propagating components of a diagram $D:n\to t$.

Let $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ be the $R$-span of the basis diagrams $D:n\to t$ with $\operatorname{prop}(D)<t$. Define the **Temperley–Lieb link-state standard module**

$$W_{n,t}(R,\delta):=M_R(n,t)/M_R^{<t}(n,t).$$

Write $T_{n,t}$ for the set of diagrams in $\mathcal D(n,t)$ with exactly $t$ propagating components. The cosets of these diagrams form an $R$-basis of $W_{n,t}$. Identifying each diagram with its bottom arcs and defects gives a partial matching of the $n$ ordered bottom sites, with the additional condition that the $t$ unpaired sites are joined to the ordered top sites by noncrossing propagating strands. In particular, no defect lies inside an arc. The unpaired sites are called **defects**. Thus $t$ is the defect or through-line number; in sources using $p$ for the number of arcs, $p=(n-t)/2$.

The intended right action of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$, where $x\in M_R(n,t)$, $a\in M_R(n,n)$, and $x\circ a$ stacks $x$ above $a$. The submodule $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ is stable under this action, so it descends to $W_{n,t}$; the complete well-definedness argument is [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-module-action-is-well-defined]].

6.1 The sole basis vector of $W_{r,r}$ is $1_r$; every generator lowers propagation and thus acts by zero, and its form value on that vector is $1$. Hence $D_{r,r}=W_{r,r}$ is the stated one-dimensional module. Finally, for $n>0$ even and $\delta=0$, gluing any two perfect matchings creates at least one closed component, so $\phi_{n,0}$ is identically zero and $D_{n,0}=0$. ## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit ([[def-algebra-over-a-commutative-ring]]) and let $\delta\in R$. The object labels are the nonnegative integers $n=0,1,2,\ldots$. For labels $m,n$, place bottom points $b_1,\ldots,b_m$ and top points $t_1,\ldots,t_n$ along the rectangle from left to right on their respective edges. Their cyclic order is $t_1,\ldots,t_n,b_m,\ldots,b_1$. When $m=n=0$, the empty matching is included.

An $(m,n)$ **diagram** is a perfect matching of these $m+n$ boundary labels which is noncrossing: there are no four labels $a,b,c,d$ in cyclic order whose matched pairs are $\{a,c\}$ and $\{b,d\}$. A picture consists of disjoint arcs realizing the matching; equality is equality of the matching, so planar deformation that fixes the boundary does not change a diagram. If $m+n$ is odd, there are no such diagrams. Write $\mathcal D(m,n)$ for this set and define the $R$-module

$$M_R(m,n):=R^{(\mathcal D(m,n))},$$

the free $R$-module on the set of diagrams ([[def-free-module-on-a-set-and-standard-basis]]). In particular, its diagram basis is empty when $m+n$ is odd.

For basis diagrams $D:m\to n$ and $E:n\to p$, stack $E$ above $D$ and identify the $n$ matching boundary points. The resulting finite graph has degree two at each identified point, where degree means the number of incident arcs. Each component is a path joining two exterior boundary points or a closed cycle. Remove every cycle and multiply the remaining exterior matching by $\delta^c$, where $c$ is the number of removed cycles. Denote this output by $E\circ D$ and extend the rule $R$-bilinearly to a map $M_R(n,p)\times M_R(m,n)\to M_R(m,p)$. A following result proves closure of these operations on the diagram modules and the category axioms.

The matching $1_n:n\to n$ pairs each bottom point to the top point directly above it. Horizontal juxtaposition, with the left diagram placed first, defines $m\otimes m'=m+m'$ on object labels and $D\otimes D'$ on basis diagrams; extend it $R$-bilinearly to the modules. A following result proves that these operations give a strict monoidal category.

For $1\le i<n$, let $d_i\in M_R(n,n)$ be the diagram with a cap joining top points $i,i+1$, a cup joining bottom points $i,i+1$, and vertical through strands at every other position. Define $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ to be the $R$-module $M_R(n,n)$ with bilinear multiplication $xy:=x\circ y$ and distinguished element $1_n$. A following result proves that it is a unital associative $R$-algebra and identifies it with the endomorphism algebra at object $n$.

The left factor is stacked above the right factor. The loop value is $\delta$; no invertibility or nonzero condition on $\delta$ is part of these data.

Use the digits and place values in [[def-temperley-lieb-spencer-digit-support]], and write $N+1=\sum_{j=0}^r n_js_j$ with $n_r>0$. When $\ell<\infty$, each signed expression $\sum_j\varepsilon_jn_js_j-1$ with $\varepsilon_r=1$ lies in $[0,N]$, has parity $N$, and determines its signs at every nonzero digit uniquely. Thus the support has $2^h$ elements, where $h$ is the number of nonzero digits below $r$.

For $0\le v\le u$, the specialized quantum binomial $B_{u,v}(\delta)$ is nonzero exactly when each mixed-radix digit of $v$ is at most the corresponding digit of $u$. In characteristic zero this uses the two digits with places $1,\ell$; if $\ell=\infty$, every such binomial is nonzero.

For any $0<k\le r$, changing all signs at indices less than $k$ reflects the corresponding support element about the wall $H-1$, where $H=\sum_{j\ge k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ is a positive multiple of $s_k$. In particular, writing $L=\sum_{j<k}\varepsilon_jn_js_j$ gives the pair $H+L-1,H-L-1$ and $|L|<s_k$.

Let $a,b,c$ belong to this support, and suppose their sets of negative nonzero digits satisfy $A\subseteq B\subseteq C$. Then $a\ge b\ge c$ and the specialized quantum binomial
$$B_{(a-c)/2,(a-b)/2}(\delta)$$
is nonzero. Here $B$ denotes the polynomial quantum binomial of [[lem-temperley-lieb-quantum-binomial-digit-criterion]]. If $\ell=\infty$, the same last assertion holds for the only triple $a=b=c=N$.

consumer_interface:
## Statement

Write $[j]_T$ for the polynomial recurrence $[0]_T=0,[1]_T=1,[j+1]_T=T[j]_T-[j-1]_T$. For a monic diagram $x:a\to b$, bend its $b$ output points around the right edge in reverse order to form a matching on $a+b$ points. Its nesting forest $F(x)$ consists of its $(a+b)/2$ arcs, ordered by containment. For an arc $e$, let $c(e)$ be the number of arcs inside it, counting itself. Define the polynomial hook weight
$$h_F(T)=\frac{[|F|]_T!}{\prod_{e\in F}[c(e)]_T}.$$
For $a\ge b$ of the same parity, define the nonzero vector
$$v_{a,b}=\sum_{x:a\to b\text{ monic}}h_{F(x)}(-\delta)x\in W_{a,b}.$$
Its coefficient on the diagram whose bent forest is a chain is $1$.

For $a\ge b\ge c$ of the same parity, composition modulo propagation less than $c$ satisfies
$$v_{a,b}\circ v_{b,c}=B_{(a-c)/2,(a-b)/2}(-\delta)v_{a,c}.$$
Composition here means attaching the indicated linear combinations of monic diagrams, in source-to-target order.

Let $s_k$ be an available finite place value of [[def-temperley-lieb-spencer-digit-support]]. If $b<a<b+2s_k$ and $a+b+2$ is divisible by $2s_k$, then postcomposition by $v_{a,b}$ induces a nonzero module homomorphism $W_{n,a}\to W_{n,b}$ for every $n\ge a$ of the same parity.

## Definition

Let $R$ be a commutative ring with unit, let $\delta\in R$, and let $n\ge0$. Let $t$ be an integer with $0\le t\le n$ and $n-t$ even. The diagram module $M_R(n,t)$ has $n$ bottom boundary points and $t$ top boundary points, with stacking and loop removal as in [[def-temperley-lieb-diagram-category]]. A component of a basis diagram is **propagating** if it meets both the bottom and top boundaries. Write $\operatorname{prop}(D)$ for the number of propagating components of a diagram $D:n\to t$.

Let $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ be the $R$-span of the basis diagrams $D:n\to t$ with $\operatorname{prop}(D)<t$. Define the **Temperley–Lieb link-state standard module**

$$W_{n,t}(R,\delta):=M_R(n,t)/M_R^{<t}(n,t).$$

Write $T_{n,t}$ for the set of diagrams in $\mathcal D(n,t)$ with exactly $t$ propagating components. The cosets of these diagrams form an $R$-basis of $W_{n,t}$. Identifying each diagram with its bottom arcs and defects gives a partial matching of the $n$ ordered bottom sites, with the additional condition that the $t$ unpaired sites are joined to the ordered top sites by noncrossing propagating strands. In particular, no defect lies inside an arc. The unpaired sites are called **defects**. Thus $t$ is the defect or through-line number; in sources using $p$ for the number of arcs, $p=(n-t)/2$.

The intended right action of $\mathrm{TL}_n(R,\delta)$ is $x\cdot a=[x\circ a]$, where $x\in M_R(n,t)$, $a\in M_R(n,n)$, and $x\circ a$ stacks $x$ above $a$. The submodule $M_R^{<t}(n,t)$ is stable under this action, so it descends to $W_{n,t}$; the complete well-definedness argument is [[lem-temperley-lieb-link-state-module-action-is-well-defined]].

consumer_fact_uses: 2.1 We first use loop value $-T$. Consider matchings with a fixed finite number $d$ of cups on a half-infinite ordered row, with all sufficiently far-left sites propagating. A diagram is encoded by the $d$ right cup endpoints, numbered from the right starting at $1$: scanning from right to left, a listed site opens a cup and the next unpaired unlisted site closes the most recent cup; unlisted sites with no open cup propagate. Thus every $d$-element subset of the positive integers encodes exactly one matching. Hook weights are unchanged by adding more leftmost propagating strands, because bending one more such strand adds a root above the entire old forest and cancels its new numerator factor. We may consequently form the formal series $V_d$ of these matchings with their hook weights. Every fixed output coefficient after a local generator or cup attachment involves finitely many terms: only its finitely many cups and the nearest exposed propagating strand can be reconnected. All operations below are defined coefficient by coefficient. [F1, step 1.1, construct, algebra]

3.1 We prove that every local generator kills $V_d$. Fix an output matching $D$ with its simple cup at sites $i,i+1$, and remove that cup to obtain a gap $J$ in $D^-$. A line is exposed to $J$ if an arc from $J$ to an interior point of that line can avoid all other lines. Replacing that line by two lines ending at $i$ and $i+1$ is its nip at $J$. Exactly $D$ itself and these nipped diagrams are the preimages contributing to the coefficient of $D$: a generator changes only the two lines meeting its sites, while the converse reconnection recovers each nip. A line exposed on both sides is nipped only once. Therefore the coefficient is $C_D=-[2]_T h(D)+\sum_{e\text{ exposed to }J}h(\operatorname{nip}_J(e)).$ This enumeration includes loops through the first term and all reconnection terms with coefficient $1$. [F1, step 1.1, step 2.1, algebra]

6.2 We check when the finite candidate $v_{a,b}$ is killed by every generator. Put $d=(a-b)/2$ and $M=(a+b)/2+1$. The cancellation of steps 3.1–5.1 applies unchanged whenever an enclosing arc or a propagating strand is exposed to the left of the distinguished cup. Only the remaining case has a missing nip: the distinguished cup is not enclosed by another cup, and there is no propagating strand to its left. Number the original input sites $1,\ldots,a$ and let the distinguished cup be $(i,i+1)$. Then every site $1,\ldots,i-1$ is paired within that interval, so $i$ is odd. Add a new leftmost input site $0$ and a new first output site, joined by a propagating strand. Remove $(i,i+1)$ and nip that new strand at its gap, producing the cup $(0,i)$ and a strand from $i+1$ to the new output site. This is the unique additional contributing diagram. Its bent matching has $(a+1+b+1)/2=M$ edges. The new cup $(0,i)$ and the $(i-1)/2$ original cups inside it form a separate tree with $t=(i+1)/2$ edges. Since the original diagram had these $t-1$ cups and the distinguished cup, $1\le t\le d$. Every other edge lies to its right, including the bent strand beginning at $i+1$, so no edge of this tree is comparable with an edge of the remaining forest. Any common roots introduced by auxiliary bending of additional strands cancel as in step 2.1 before this split is counted. By step 1.1 its hook weight consequently factors as $B_{M,t}(T)$ times the polynomial hook weights of those two parts. The uncanceled coefficient is the negative of this missing hook weight. For $a=3,b=1,i=1$, the missing matching has a one-edge component and a two-edge chain, giving $B_{3,1}(T)=[3]_T$, whose negative agrees with the direct coefficient $1-T^2$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 3.1, step 5.1, algebra]

7.1 Attaching $V_{s-r}$ to a half-infinite diagram with $r$ cups defines a map to the diagrams with $s$ cups. It commutes with all generators: ordinary surviving diagram compositions commute by associativity, loop terms have the same scalar on both sides, and when a generator joins two propagating strands the failure coefficient is exactly the vanishing coefficient of steps 3.1–5.1 after suppressing unchanged cups. Composing two attachment maps attaches a formal vector with the sum of their cup counts. This vector is killed by every generator, so step 6.1 makes it a scalar multiple of the corresponding $V$. The scalar is obtained on the fully nested output diagram. Its only monic factorization first inserts its inner $u$ cups and then its remaining $v$ cups. Indeed every cup in the first factor must be a cup of the nested output, and choosing any cup forces every cup inside it to be chosen too, since a defect cannot lie inside a cup. With exactly $u$ cups, this selects precisely the $u$ innermost cups; the remaining through strands have their uniquely forced order. After bending, the first factor has two chains of lengths $u,v$ below successive common roots and hence weight $B_{u+v,u}(T)$; the second factor has a chain forest and weight $1$. This gives scalar $B_{u+v,u}(T)$. Restricting the attachment maps to a finite row and discarding diagrams using a site beyond its left boundary preserves this composition identity, because further cup insertion never removes such a site. With $u=(a-b)/2,v=(b-c)/2$, this proves the asserted finite candidate-composition identity over loop value $-T$. [F1, F2, step 1.1, step 2.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, algebra]

8.1 Finally, if a linear combination $v\in W_{a,b}$ is killed by all generators, every adjacent cap at the $a$ inputs kills it modulo propagation less than $b$. This follows by factoring the generator as cup followed by cap: insertion of that cup is injective on the relevant monic diagram basis, so zero after insertion implies zero before insertion. Every diagram $n\to a$ of propagation less than $a$ has a cup on its $a$-boundary, and an innermost such cup is adjacent; factoring it off shows that its postcomposition with $v$ is zero modulo propagation less than $b$. Postcomposition consequently descends from the quotient $W_{n,a}$ to $W_{n,b}$ and commutes with the diagram action. Nonzeroness for every $n\ge a$ follows by choosing a monic diagram $z:n\to a$ with a left retraction, by [F4]: because $a>b\ge0$, one has $a>0$, and the shifted adjacent-cup construction gives this retraction over every field without division. Composing a putative zero $zv$ with the retraction would give $v=0$, a contradiction. Step 7.2 supplies precisely this annihilated nonzero $v$ under the stated wall hypotheses. Together with step 7.1 and the substitution in step 7.2, this proves all conclusions. [F1, F4, step 7.1, step 7.2, algebra] ∎

## Statement

For $0\le k\le n$, let $G_{n,k}(Q)$ be the polynomial $\sum_w Q^{\operatorname{inv}(w)}$, summed over binary words with $k$ ones and $n-k$ zeros, where $\operatorname{inv}(w)$ counts pairs with a one to the left of a zero. There is a unique polynomial $B_{n,k}(T)\in\mathbb Z[T]$ such that

$$B_{n,k}(q+q^{-1})=q^{-k(n-k)}G_{n,k}(q^2).$$

It agrees as a rational-function identity with $[n]!/([k]![n-k]!)$; its value at a specialized loop parameter is the polynomial value, without division by vanishing factorials.

For a field $K$, $\delta\in K$, recurrence quantum characteristic $\ell$, and $p=\operatorname{char}K$, every $B_{n,k}(\delta)$ for $0\le k\le n$ is nonzero exactly as follows: if $\ell=\infty$, at every finite $n$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p>0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell p^{i-1}-1$ with $i\ge1$ and $1\le a<p$; if $\ell<\infty$ and $p=0$, when $n<\ell$ or $n=a\ell-1$ for a positive integer $a$.
